sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: In this lesson you use three skills you already know: the passive with *ser* (B1 Unit 18), reported speech and *según* (B1 Unit 13), and the choice between an infinitive and *que* + subjunctive (B2 Unit 4). Together they let you write a short, careful text about a community and what it says it wants.

sections.title: Three skills, one text
rows: El café es cultivado por pequeñas familias.
passive with *ser*: the participle agrees with *café*
Los representantes dijeron que defenderían el bosque.
Los cantones quieren defender el bosque.
same person wants and acts: infinitive
Los cantones quieren que el Gobierno respete el voto.

items.spanish: Los bosques comunales son cuidados por los cantones.
items.english: The communal forests are looked after by the cantons.

items.spanish: Según sus representantes, las autoridades sirven sin sueldo.
items.english: According to their representatives, the authorities serve without a salary.

items.spanish: Dijeron que querían que se respetara el voto.
items.english: They said that they wanted the vote to be respected.

items.spanish: Las cooperativas quieren vender el café a un precio justo.
items.english: The cooperatives want to sell the coffee at a fair price.

sections.content: Ask who does what. If the person who wants and the person who acts are the same, use the infinitive (*quieren defender*); if they differ, use *que* + subjunctive (*quieren que el Gobierno respete*). After a past verb the subjunctive moves back too: *querían que se respetara*.
